probes.question: True or false: in the scar study, the scar was still visible when volunteers met the other person.
What is the spotlight effect?
options: Believing you are noticed more than you are

image.alt: Rows of black stage spotlights on a lighting truss seen from below inside a theatre.

panels.text: 1980. Volunteers had makeup applied to look like a prominent facial scar, and checked it in a mirror.
The makeup artist then added a cream, said to stop the scar drying out. In fact, it removed the scar entirely, and the volunteers did not know.
They chatted with another person, then rated how they had been treated. They reported being treated significantly differently: more tense, less eye contact, more patronising.
The scar was gone. The difference was entirely their self-consciousness. This is the spotlight effect: believing we are noticed more than we really are.
